title: Compatibility ledger and pinning policy for IaC modules/providers in Private VPC
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: Private (VPC) customers run a curated set of Terraform modules and providers that must remain stable across provider upgrades (aws, azurerm, google). We've had two incidents in the last year where upstream provider changes unexpectedly changed plan outcomes in customer tenants. Goal: produce a single-source compatibility ledger (human + machine readable) and a clear pinning policy plus automated checks that reduce upgrade surprises and make rollouts safe.
scope: 1) Compatibility ledger mapping module versions to tested provider versions, Terraform core versions, and minimal required provider feature flags. 2) Pinning policy (exact pins vs compatible ranges) tailored to module stability tiers. 3) CI gates that fail PRs introducing provider bumps unless a matrix run passes. 4) Health-checks and preflight automation for customer upgrades: plan-sanity, drift snapshot, state backup/verify. 5) Runbook for rolling upgrades and emergency rollbacks.
deliverables:
- compat-ledger.csv and compat-ledger.json stored in infra-iac/docs
- policy doc: pinning-guidelines.md (private-vpc repo)
- CI job: tf-compat-check (matrix runner across providers/terraform versions)
- Bot: tf-bump-bot draft that opens pinned-version bump PRs with matrix results
- Runbook: upgrades/preflight/postflight checklist with commands and safety gates
- Migration notes for customers for major provider bumps
approach:
- Audit current modules in private-vpc registry and capture current consumer usage patterns (seq length of TF plans, common resources).
- Assign stability tier to each module (stable / evolving / experimental) based on churn and test coverage.
- For stable modules: exact provider pins for patch-level and minor-level pins only after matrix validation. For evolving: minor-range pins (~> semver) with CI promotion.
- Implement tf-compat-check GitHub Action that runs 'terraform init && terraform plan' across a matrix of provider versions and terraform versions using example fixture workspaces for each module.
- Add preflight script `iac/preflight/checks.sh` that runs remote plan validation, state snapshot to S3 with checksum, and a lightweight drift detector.
- Add automatic tagging in ledger for 'deprecation-window' and 'rollback-tested'.
acceptance_criteria:
- compat-ledger exists for top-20 modules and is surfaced in docs.
- tf-compat-check action runs on bump PRs and blocks merges when matrix has regressions.
- Rollback runbook validated by staging dry-run.
- At least one provider bump successfully promoted through canary->staging->prod with no customer incidents during rollout.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Matrix combinatorics blow up CI time. Mitigation: sample by representative providers (AWS/GCP) and limit to supported region/versions; run full matrix on nightly.
- Risk: Pinning too strictly prevents security patches. Mitigation: emergency security bump path with mandatory smoke tests.
- Risk: State format drift for Terraform versions. Mitigation: include state migration test in matrix and snapshot/rollback procedure.
notes:
We intentionally separate human-readable ledger (CSV) and machine-readable JSON for automation. Ledger rows: module, module_version, terraform_version_tested, provider_name, provider_version_tested, stability_tier, last_tested, test_sha, rollback_steps_reference.
Prototype tests live in infra-iac/.github/workflows/tf-compat-check.yml. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRIV-VPC-compat-design (internal).
